description: Turns one voltage into eight, fanned out from it by a spacing you set, with a tilt that bends the spacing and a random offset per voice

params.text: Chooses which way the eight fan out from the input voltage: downward from it, centred on it, or upward from it
Sets the gap between one voice and the next, -1.4V to +1.4V, with the eight voltages collapsing onto each other at zero
Scales the SPREAD CV input before it is added to the SPREAD knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Bends the spacing so the gaps grow towards the ends or towards the middle, -1 to +1 with no bend at the centre; the bend is scaled by SPREAD
Scales the TILT CV input before it is added to the TILT knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Sets how much of its own random offset each voice is given, -1 to +1; each voice keeps the number it was given until a new set is drawn
Scales the RANDOM CV input before it is added to the RANDOM knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to +10V after the gain, so the eight voltages can be produced with nothing patched in at all
Scales the input before anything else, from -1 through zero to +1, so a setting below zero inverts it; it comes up at +1

inputs.text: Moves SPREAD after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
Moves TILT after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
A rising edge draws a fresh random number for every one of the eight voices; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
Moves RANDOM after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
The single voltage the eight are built from; only the first channel of a cable is read

outputs.text: The eight voltages as an eight-channel polyphonic cable, voice one first
The same eight voltages as an eight-channel polyphonic cable, in the opposite order

notes: the random numbers are held until a rising edge arrives at TRIG, and they are saved with the patch, so a patch reloads with the same fan-out it had.
fanning upward adds each voice's random offset, fanning downward subtracts it, and the centred setting spreads it either side of the voice.
with nothing patched into INPUT the module produces eight voltages anyway, built from the OFFSET knob alone.

inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
